svg.title: Unstuck breaks a repeated decision loop: a receipt removes the dead end before the next choice.
svg.desc: Top: BEFORE UNSTUCK. A synthetic order report returns zero rows; each call has one diagnostic read. The memoryless control makes three independent calls on the same synthetic case. Each chooses inspect_pipeline, spends one read, finds that the partition arrived, and returns unresolved: 3 of 3 unresolved. Each circuit represents a separate bounded call, not a literal infinite loop. Bottom: WITH UNSTUCK. Run 1 happens once: one inference, one read, 21.6 seconds client time, unresolved. The deterministic verifier stores a disposition_unchanged Decision Receipt. Run 1 is not saved. The paper receipt travels into Run 2, where an exact match lets the controller preclude only inspect_pipeline before the first Decider request and before any read. The two remaining diagnostics and request_review keep their original order. The receipt never chooses a tool. The same Decider makes one fresh choice, inspect_schema_keys; one read reaches verified repair and completed. No second Decider call. Optimized Run 2: one inference, 26.6 seconds. Superseded post-choice Run 2: two inferences, 54.8 seconds. Observed Run 2 client latency difference: 28.2 seconds, 51.4% lower. n = 1, same synthetic case, each proof once. No dollar savings measured. No rate, significance, accuracy, model learning, novelty, production readiness or guaranteed benefit is established. The twenty-eight-second choreography shows causal order, not measured elapsed time. Reduced motion and animation failure show the full final before/after comparison, receipt stored, branch cut, and completed route.

g.text: Synthetic zero-row report / one read per call
Same case / each proof once / No dollar savings.
